horizontal_tail.name: Horizontal tail spar
horizontal_tail.model: Timoshenko beam FEA, 2 DOF/node, 21 sizing stations + Saint-Venant root-warping stress recovery
assumptions: Same solver and stations as the contract FeaResult; optimisation scales t_f and t_w linearly root→tip
Gauges clamped to Raymer minimums t_f ≥ 2.0 mm, t_w ≥ 1.5 mm
Mass is one tail half (multiply by 2)
Tail load case and planform from the tail sizing: Raymer 2ed Eqs. 14.12-14.13, C_n (p. 347), Table 4.3
horizontal_tail.convergence_note: Stations fixed by the spar sizing (21 nodes).

min_mass.rationale: The baseline root outer cap fibre at y = 0.00 m has a generous 2.323 margin under cantilever bending, allowing both root and tip gauges to be reduced to the 0.60 lower bound while keeping the margin well above 0.10.

ai_proposal.rationale: Cantilever bending moments peak at the y = 0.00 m root outer cap fibre and vanish toward the tip, so shifting mass from the lightly loaded tip (k_tip = 0.60) to the governing root zone (k_root = 1.24) maximizes the stress margin within the baseline mass budget.

max_margin.rationale: Every zone is already at minimum gauge (sheet ≥ 0.50 mm): peak σ_vM 131 MPa, margin +2.32. The part is minimum-gauge governed, so no gauge change helps; a lighter design needs thinner stock or a different section, not re-gauging.

ai_proposal.rationale: Thinning the lightly stressed outboard spar caps and web to k_tip = 0.60 and utilizing the 5% mass allowance permits thickening the governing root zone to k_root = 1.32, directly lowering peak von Mises bending and warping stress at y = 0.00 m.
